Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear ask.

Below is a short, copy-ready comparison and a list of artifacts Helios can attach to the SIG. I kept it focused on the four items the committee listed. If you want this turned into a single-page PDF we can drop into the Drive link you sent.

---
Summary (hosted | dedicated | private)

1) Data residency & retention
- Hosted: Redwood stores customer data in the region selected at sign-up. Redwood is responsible for physical storage, backups, and enforcing retention policies; Helios can configure retention via the Console and request deletions via support. Artifact: region residency statement + retention controls doc (redwood-sig-hosting-matrix-20260802.pdf).
- Dedicated: Dedicated pools are single-tenant to your organization within our cloud region; Redwood operates storage but isolation reduces co-tenancy risk. Customer controls retention; Redwood provides export and deletion tooling. Artifact: dedicated-tenant-isolation.pdf + runbook excerpt.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Helios controls physical locations and retention via their own infrastructure and policies; Redwood provides control-plane integrations but does not store customer content unless explicitly configured. Artifact: private-deployment-ops-guidance.txt + arch-diagram-hosted-dedicated-private.png.

2) Customer key management (BYOK / KMS)
- Hosted: Redwood manages encryption-at-rest keys by default; customers may enable KMS integrations (customer-managed keys in supported clouds). Artifact: kms-integration-note.txt + SOC 2 encryption controls reference.
- Dedicated: KMS options available; Redwood supports customer-provided keys for dedicated pools. Artifact: KMS config sample + network boundary doc.
- Private: Full BYOK and HSM support under customer control; Redwood's control plane can be configured to use customer keys or not store keys at all. Artifact: private-kms-architecture.pdf.

3) Audit log access & export
- Hosted: Audit logs are produced by Redwood and can be exported via API or added as part of a logging export integration (S3/Cloud Storage). Redwood retains logs per the SLAs. Artifact: audit-log-export-spec.md + sample logs (redacted).
- Dedicated: Logs are isolated per tenant and can be forwarded to customer-managed sinks; retention configurable.
- Private: Logging is under Helios' control; Redwood supplies hooks for the control plane and recommended log schemas.

4) Legal / subpoena / e-discovery handling
- Hosted: Redwood receives legal requests through our legal team; Redwood will notify customers per our policy unless prohibited; data access complies with our transparency/security policies. Artifact: legal-requests-process.pdf (SOC 2 section references).
- Dedicated: Same as hosted, with additional contractual options for customer notifications and response playbooks.
- Private: Helios controls the data; Redwood only responds if contractually authorized to act on behalf of the customer.

---
Suggested attachments for the SIG spreadsheet: 1) redwood-sig-hosting-matrix-20260802.pdf (summary table), 2) arch-diagram-hosted-dedicated-private.png, 3) kms-integration-note.txt, 4) SOC2-report-excerpt.pdf (SOC 2: CC6–CC8 encryption & logging).

If you want, Marissa can add the two-line narrative text for each free-text field. Rishi can confirm the SOC 2 references are correct. I copied them here to speed things up.

Cheers,
